run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-15T11:41:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert opened on the fraud-detection error rate (the alert payload states 0.0222, i.e. 'above 0'). In the telemetry I could read (metrics until about 11:10–11:12Z, traces until about 11:02–11:05Z), the only ERROR-status span series belonging to fraud-detection are gRPC client spans to flagd: ten counts of span_name=flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with span_kind=SPAN_KIND_CLIENT and status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, plus two of flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt with STATUS_CODE_ERROR; the service's other series are STATUS_CODE_UNSET (orders receive 221, orders process 230, resolve 4, ResolveInt 2). Jaeger confirms that the EventStream spans carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) with durations of about 594–602 s, so the long-lived flagd event-stream subscription is recorded as an error each time it ends on its ~600 s deadline; two flagd-side spans of the same stream carry otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'. The identical EventStream ERROR pattern exists for ad (error count 10; five spans with code 4) and for recommendation (seven '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' errors), so the condition is not unique to fraud-detection. A small absolute number of stream-timeout error spans against about 469 total spans yields a ratio of about 2.2–2.6% error spans, which matches the alert's magnitude. fraud-detection itself looks healthy on its own request path: its orders receive/orders process spans show no error rows, the deployment has 10/10 ready replicas, all ten pods are Running with restartCount 0 (started 10:45:38–10:48:41Z), and flagd's pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts. The checkout/frontend errors belong to a different failure (shipping /get-quote 'EOF'), so they do not evidence fraud-detection impact. Two Kafka pods restarted (exit 1) at 10:52:02Z and 10:56:59Z, but the fraud-detection error spans are flagd gRPC streams, not Kafka consumption, and the orders spans show no errors. The exact alert evaluation at 11:41:36Z cannot be verified: metric samples stop around 11:10–11:15Z and trace samples around 11:02–11:05Z, and the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus, so its expression and window are unknown.

claims.text: Only two metric families exist for service_name="fraud-detection" in this Prometheus: traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so any error-rate signal for fraud-detection comes from traced spans, not from HTTP/RPC request metrics.

At 11:10:00Z the fraud-detection span counters were: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 10, flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 2, ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 2, resolve STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 4, orders process STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 230, orders receive STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 221 (10 + 2 = 12 error-counted spans out of 469 total spans).

The ERROR series for span flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream on fraud-detection are span_kind=SPAN_KIND_CLIENT spans exported by the otel-collector spanmetrics connector from the per-pod exporters (many distinct exported_instance values), i.e. they are fraud-detection's client spans to flagd.

Jaeger returns 10 fraud-detection spans for operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, durations 594101234-601796702 microseconds (~594-602 s), starts 10:50:13Z-10:52:01Z; the same traces' flagd-side spans show 7 with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and 2 with error=true plus otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

The EventStream ERROR counter for fraud-detection rose from 1 at 11:01:00Z to 3 at 11:02:00Z, 7 at 11:03:00Z and 10 at 11:04:00Z while orders receive UNSET rose 155 -> 181 -> 221 and orders process UNSET 164 -> 190 -> 230, i.e. the error burst coincided with a small ~450-span population.

The fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_ERROR series reached 2 at 11:00:00Z and stayed 2 through 11:11:00Z, while the ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_UNSET series stayed at 2, so two flagd ResolveInt client spans were counted as errors around 10:59-11:00Z.

fraud-detection's own request-handling spans carried no errors: the trace sample for the service shows 30 'orders receive' and 30 'orders process' spans all with status not_recorded and 0 error_rows, durations 1.9 ms-98.9 ms.

Kubernetes state at query time: deployment fraud-detection is 10/10 replicas available and ready; its 10 pods are all Running and ready with restartCount 0, owned by ReplicaSet fraud-detection-9fb7d885b, started 10:45:38Z-10:48:41Z; the flagd deployment is 1/1 ready and pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx started 10:47:30Z with restartCount 0.

The same flagd EventStream ERROR signature occurs outside fraud-detection: the ad service has 5 sampled EventStream spans with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and durations ~597-604 s, and the cumulative error counters show ad = 10 and recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' = 7 versus fraud-detection = 10.

The checkout/frontend errors present in the same window are caused by shipping, not fraud-detection: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and otel.status_description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post "http://shipping:8080/get-quote": EOF', and no fraud-detection span appears in that error trace.

Primary driver of the firing alert: fraud-detection's long-lived flagd EventStream subscriptions end at their ~600 s deadline and are recorded as ERROR client spans (rpc.grpc.status_code=4 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), 10 of them in the burst at 11:00-11:04Z; with only ~450-470 total spans for the service a 10-12 error-span count gives an error ratio of about 0.022-0.026, matching the alert's nonzero reading.

Secondary candidate inside the same cause: flagd itself closes some event streams on a server-side timeout (2 of 9 flagd-side EventStream spans carry otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout' with rpc.grpc.status_code=4), and a single flagd replica serves the whole demo, so server-side stream timeouts/keepalive limits are a plausible contributor to the client-observed errors; the relevant flagd configuration could not be read.

A distinct, smaller contributor: 2 fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt client spans are counted STATUS_CODE_ERROR around 10:59-11:00Z, which would be genuine flag-evaluation call failures; their cause is unknown because no trace or error detail for them was returned.

Metric coverage ends before the alert time: the fraud-detection metric queries report source_end_at 11:10:00Z and 11:12:00Z and the trace queries report source_end_at 11:01:59Z and 11:05:40Z, while the alert is anchored at 11:41:36Z, so no sample in this Run shows the state at alert evaluation.

increase() over these counters does not reflect the raw counter movement: sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[300s])) returned 0 at every step 11:03-11:11Z while the raw summed counter for the same series rose from 1 to 10 between 11:01 and 11:04Z, so the alert rule's window/expression cannot be reconstructed from this data.

Two of the ten kafka pods had crashed and restarted during the window: kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w last terminated with reason Error, exitCode 1 at 10:56:59Z (restartCount 3) and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr at 10:52:02Z (restartCount 1); all ten kafka pods are now Running and ready.

Kafka pod crashes were considered as the cause of the fraud-detection error rate and rejected: the only ERROR-status spans attributed to fraud-detection are flagd gRPC client spans (EventStream, ResolveInt), its Kafka-fed operations 'orders receive'/'orders process' show 451 spans with no error rows, and the two Kafka restarts ended at 10:52:02Z/10:56:59Z before the error-span burst completed at 11:00-11:04Z; Kafka container logs were not readable, so its own error cause stays unknown and is not counted as fraud-detection impact.

A crash, eviction or restart of fraud-detection was considered and rejected as the trigger: all 10 fraud-detection pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination state, having started 10:45:38Z-10:48:41Z, and the deployment reports 10/10 available/ready.

Inspect the RequestErrorRate alert rule where it is actually defined (Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files outside this target) and check whether it counts long-lived streaming spans such as flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; if so, filter streaming deadline spans out of the error numerator or require a sustained ratio rather than 'above 0'.

Review flagd server stream timeout/keepalive settings and the flagd provider stream deadline used by fraud-detection (and the other demo services showing the same EventStream errors), since the observed spans are ~600 s streaming calls that end in DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and some flagd-side spans report 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'; also confirm the flagd replica count is adequate for the subscription load of the demo's services.

Re-derive the error ratio at 11:41:36Z from a data source that retains samples past 11:15Z (or from Alertmanager's own rule evaluation) before treating the warning as a live condition, and read the flagd and fraud-detection container logs from a log store that still retains the 11:00-11:05Z window.

gaps: No metric samples exist after about 11:10-11:12Z and no trace spans after about 11:02-11:05Z in this target, so the alert's stated value 0.0222 at its 11:41:36Z start is unverified; the alert JSON itself is not tool evidence.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no data (status no_data), so the rule expression, lookback window and current alert state could not be inspected.

fraud-detection and flagd pod logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned no lines and status no_data for pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l (containers wait-for-kafka, fraud-detection) and for pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (containers init-config, flagd, flagd-ui), so application-level error text is unknown.

No trace was returned for the 2 fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans (the operation-filtered search returned no data), so their error detail and status code are unknown.

flagd has no spanmetrics series under service_name="flagd" in this Prometheus (get_metric_names returned no data for that selector), so flagd-side error and latency rates could not be measured, only sampled from Jaeger.

A pod query filtered by label selector app=fraud-detection returned no data, although the deployment's fraud-detection pods exist; the pod-label value used by this cluster is therefore not confirmed, and pod-level conclusions rest on the deployment-replica and name-based queries.
No Kubernetes events were returned for fraud-detection or flagd objects (only events timestamped 11:00:55Z-11:03:59Z were available), and current object state cannot show the cluster at 11:41:36Z.
The change_history integration is not available, so no configuration change (for example a flagd stream timeout or a fraud-detection deployment change) can be checked.

The Jaeger results are biased samples limited by the backend (searches returned as many traces as requested, flagged incomplete), so counts of EventStream errors from traces are a sample, not a complete failure count.
Kafka container logs were not readable and the two Kafka container restarts (exit code 1) are unexplained by this evidence; they are recorded as a change in the window, not as fraud-detection impact.
next_steps: Locate the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition in the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule configuration and determine whether flagd EventStream deadline spans are included in its error numerator.
Check flagd's stream timeout/keepalive configuration and the flagd provider deadline configured in the demo services, including whether one flagd replica is sufficient for the subscription load.
Verify from a data source with retention past 11:15Z whether the fraud-detection error ratio was still ~0.022 at 11:41:36Z and whether new EventStream deadline errors appeared after 11:04Z.
Retrieve flagd and fraud-detection application logs from a log store that retains 10:50-11:05Z to confirm the client-side deadline and server-side timeout messages.
Confirm the cause of the two Kafka container restarts (exit code 1 at 10:52:02Z and 10:56:59Z) separately; they are not tied to fraud-detection's error spans by this evidence.
